title: AI Zero → Builder
goal: Total beginner → shipped your first AI-assisted thing, understanding what you're actually doing.

steps.title: Understand what AI actually is
steps.description: Read the plain-English mental model — text prediction, not a database. It fixes your expectations for everything after.

steps.title: Pick your first chat assistant
steps.description: Try one free chat app (ChatGPT, claude.ai, Gemini, or Z.ai). They're all LLMs with different accents — pick whichever loads fastest for you.

steps.title: Prompt practice: 5 prompts that teach more than a course
steps.description: Ask it to: explain today's news in simple words, quiz you on a topic you're studying, rewrite your last email politely, plan a weekend trip, and argue the other side of an opinion you hold. Notice what makes answers better or worse.

steps.title: Make one tiny real thing
steps.description: Use the chat to help you create something you'll actually use — a study helper, a weekly meal plan, a birthday plan. Real usage teaches you AI faster than any tutorial.

steps.title: Learn the words
steps.description: Skim the glossary. Token, context, prompt — the vocabulary makes every future article readable.

steps.title: Ready for the next level
steps.description: You now know what AI feels like. Path 3 (Connect Any API) turns 'I use it' into 'I build with it'.

title: Developer Basics — the 'weird internet tools'
goal: Terminal, git, GitHub, and files stop being scary — the survival kit every tutorial assumes you already have.

steps.title: Terminal 101
steps.description: Open it, learn five commands (dir/ls, cd, mkdir, echo, cls/clear), and win the 'black window' fear forever.

steps.title: Install VS Code
steps.description: The editor everyone uses. Learn Ctrl-P, Ctrl-Shift-P, and the built-in terminal — those three keys run your life after.

steps.title: Git basics: save-points for code
steps.description: git init, git add, git commit — a time machine in three commands. You only need save-points today; branches can wait.

steps.title: GitHub account + first repo
steps.description: Push your first repo (this is literally how HELPINhex itself started). Star three tools you find interesting.

steps.title: JSON and .env
steps.description: The two file formats that run everything: data travels as JSON, secrets live in .env. Read both guides.

steps.title: Where to ask for help
steps.description: How to read a README, search GitHub issues, and ask a good question — the most underrated skill in tech.

title: Connect Any API
goal: From 'I have no idea what an API is' to a working chatbot you wrote — the single most useful beginner skill in AI.
prereqs: developer-basics (or: you can open a terminal)

steps.title: Understand APIs
steps.description: The restaurant analogy, JSON, endpoints — the mental model that makes every tutorial make sense.

steps.title: Get a free key
steps.description: Create an OpenRouter account and key — your universal ticket to hundreds of models.

steps.title: Make your first API call
steps.description: One terminal command, a real reply from a real model, and the complete error hall of fame explained.

steps.title: Build a tiny chatbot
steps.description: Wrap that call in a 20-line script that keeps conversation history. Congratulations — that's the skeleton of every AI app.

steps.title: Keep your keys safe
steps.description: The five habits that keep your bills boring — read before you build anything bigger.

steps.title: The local alternative
steps.description: Run models on your own machine with Ollama — free, private, offline. It even speaks the same API format.

steps.title: What's next: making AI accurate
steps.description: Preview of RAG — how to make AI answer from YOUR facts instead of guessing. That's where real projects live.
